newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Belgian shares find recent gains hard to hold.
newsitem.headline: Belgian shares find recent gains hard to hold.

text.p: Belgian shares slid again on Tuesday as investors continued to play it safe and book profits on recent market gains, dealers said.
"I think it's definitely a bit of profit-taking. There remains unease that the market had moved too much, too quickly," Wim Van Dyke of Generale Bank brokerage unit G-Securities said.

The Bel-20 index, which added 150 points last week in a continuous stream of record-breaking sessions, gave up 27.37 points, or 1.15 percent, to end at 2,360.03 points. Losses deepened late in the day as bond yields started rising and Wall Street opened softer.
On Monday the Bel-20 index had lost 12.96 points.
"The issues which are suffering most are those that have performed really well -- Union Miniere, Barco and Kredietbank," Van Dyke said.
UM lost 2.41 percent at 3,235 francs, Barco 3.06 percent at 6,650 francs, Kredietbank 4.68 percent lower at 14,750 francs.

Dealers did not believe the approach of the expiry of June Bel-20 options and futures was a factor. "When the market is bullish, people should normally be long," one said. "In any case, futures don't lead cash in Belgium."
